Google Flow and Krea are the two free tiers that clearly publish text-to-video as of Nov 17, 2026. Flow gives 50 credits a day, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips at 720p if every credit goes to Lite. Which free AI tools turn text into video?

Google Flow and Krea are the two free tiers that clearly publish text-to-video as of Nov 17, 2026. Google Flow’s help pages list Text to Video for people without a paid Google AI plan on both Omni Flash 1.2 (3 to 10 seconds) and Veo 3.1 Lite (4, 6, or 8 seconds at 720p), paid for from 50 credits a day. Krea says a free account can open its Video Tool, type a prompt, pick one of the free video models, and generate, using 100 compute units a day with no credit card and no watermark. Dreamina’s own guide says you can make a video from text with its free daily credits, 120 a day in the US, but it does not publish what a clip costs. Grok says it is free to try, with no published free video allowance. Pika Free has 0 monthly credits, Runway’s 125 credits are one-time, and Luma has no public free plan. Everything else is unknown.

How does free text-to-video AI work, and what does this page cover?

Text-to-video AI generates a short clip from a written description alone, so the model decides how everything looks. This guide lists a tool as a yes only when an official page says, or clearly shows, that a text prompt can make a video on the free tier. Free tiers are paid for in daily credits, one-time credits, or compute units, and a clip count is given only when the vendor publishes both the allowance and what a clip costs. Quality scores come from Artificial Analysis’s text-to-video board and are quoted only for models a free tier or a priced row actually offers. Scores on this page are copied from that board, as opened Nov 17, 2026, with their 95% interval and rank range. This page does not invent scores, and it does not rank free tiers by Elo. Artificial Analysis AA-Video-T2V v2.1 leaderboard ranks models on generating video with audio from a text prompt, using Elo from pairwise human preference votes.

    Which free text-to-video option is best for each use?

    For a daily allowance you can count, and the highest published quality score we could confirm on a free allowance: Google Flow. For no credit card and no watermark: Krea Free, for personal use. For the Seedance family in a consumer app: Dreamina, with a clip count that is not published. For a watermark-free export on a $0 plan: Pika, but only after you buy a credit pack. For a one-time trial: Runway’s 125 credits. A best-for or not-for line is given only where a vendor page or a cited score supports it.

    • Google Flow. Best for: a daily allowance you can count (50 credits, about five Veo 3.1 Lite clips), and the highest published text-to-video score we could confirm on a free allowance: Gemini Omni Flash 1.2 at Elo 1151 ±14 (rank range 3–9, 5,634 samples) on Artificial Analysis AA-Video-T2V v2.1 leaderboard. Not for: a top score from Lite, since Veo 3.1 Lite is Elo 949 ±14 (rank range 26–30) on the same board; generating between roughly 9 AM–12 PM ET (6–9 AM PT) without a paid plan; or clips longer than 10 seconds. Related: Google Flow credits calculator · Veo 3.1 · Gemini Omni Flash.
    • Krea Free. Best for: no credit card and no watermark, both stated by Krea. Not for: commercial work, since Krea says videos made on the free plan are for personal use, or for Seedance 2.5 and Veo 3.1, which need Pro or higher. Krea’s AI video generator page · Krea’s pricing page. MiniMax H3 (768p) is Elo 1159 ±13 (rank range 2–7) on the same board, and Krea’s image-to-video page marks MiniMax H3 as Free plan during the current MiniMax promotion; whether it accepts a text-only prompt on Free is unknown. Related: MiniMax Hailuo model page.
    • Dreamina. Best for: the Seedance family in a consumer app with daily credits, as Dreamina states. Not for: planning a clip count ahead of time, since credits per clip are not published, or a clean file from the free example, which Dreamina’s own guide says had a watermark and no audio track. Dreamina’s text-to-video guide · Dreamina plans. Related: Seedance 2.5 model page.
    • Pika. Best for: a watermark-free export on a $0 plan once you buy a pack; Pika H3 Flex is Elo 1124 ±14 (rank range 11–15) on the same board. Not for: free clips, since Free has 0 monthly credits and no commercial license. Pika’s pricing page.
    • Runway. Best for: a single trial session on 125 one-time credits. Not for: recurring free use. Runway’s own models were not on the board read Nov 17, 2026, so their quality is unknown here. Runway’s pricing page. Related: Runway pricing per second.

    No line given. Grok Imagine, Hailuo, Wan, Kling, and Higgsfield do not publish a free text-to-video allowance on the pages we could read, so this page gives them no best-for or not-for line.

    What does text-to-video cost when the free tier runs out?

    Less than most first paid plans suggest, if you can use an API or a multi-model plan. The cheapest catalog row in the table is $0.0167 per second for Wan 3.0 on Higgsfield Ultra (annual) at 480p, audio not stated, but that row does not state input type. The lowest rate in our catalog whose vendor page states text-to-video input is $0.02 per second for Grok Imagine Video 1.5 Lite on the xAI API at 480p, audio not stated, billed per second of output. MiniMax H3 Max Turbo is $0.025 per second on fal at 480p, and Wan 3.0 is $0.035 per second on Replicate at 480p. On Google Flow, an 8-second Veo 3.1 Lite clip at 720p works out to $0.025 per second on Google AI Pro, if you use every monthly credit.     • Try the calculator. Put your clip length into the credit calculator for Veo 3.1 at 8 seconds, or the Google Flow credits calculator, to see what the paid step costs you.
    • Open the model page. Every current rate, with its source and date: Veo 3.1 · Gemini Omni Flash · Wan 3.0 · Grok Imagine.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
